clue.text: Sod all right with a political follower's flowery speech

blocks.note: sod all is slang for nothing, and nothing is the letter O
R is the standard abbreviation for right
taken as written
a follower of the British Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on a politician's grandiloquent party speech.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the wordplay to the definition. Sod all is British slang for nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Oratory is the art of public speaking, often implying an elaborate, high-flown style.

clue.text: Fruity thing, Brenda? More like the beast!

blocks.note: the ugli is a Jamaican citrus fruit
Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, Elizabeth Regina, abbreviated ER

explanation.surface: A jibe at the Queen, comparing her unfavourably with the Beast of the fairy tale.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye has long called Queen Elizabeth II 'Brenda'; ER is her royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beast of Beauty and the Beast is hideous, so being more like him means being uglier.

clue.text: (see 26ac.) A super crook?

blocks.note: surface reading: an exceptionally good criminal, a master villain
setter's reading: a super is a superintendent in the police, and crook here means dishonest, so a corrupt police officer

explanation.walkthrough: 'Super' looks like praise but is short for police superintendent; 'crook' works as the slang adjective for crooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Bent is slang for corrupt and copper slang for a police officer, so the phrase names a crooked policeman.

clue.text: (& 14dn.) Gaby's bust, grabbed by Jo – gets a lot of fingering

definitions.note: a description of the thing rather than a noun: it is something that gets fingered a great deal

indicators.note: something bust is broken, so the name's letters are smashed and rearranged
being grabbed means being held inside another's grip, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
Jo Brand is a British stand-up comedian

explanation.surface: A lurid tabloid tale of one woman groping another, Gaby's chest being much fondled.
explanation.walkthrough: Jo Brand's surname splits after its B to hold the jumbled Gaby. The fingering is a pianist's, not a groper's.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby grand is a small grand piano, played with the fingers on its keyboard.

clue.text: Politician, er, about to get a booze dispenser

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
a publican runs a pub and serves its drinks

explanation.surface: A hesitant remark about a politician who is about to be handed a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'er' is just a stammer in the surface and contributes nothing. A publican is a pub landlord, the person behind the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A Republican is a member of the US Republican Party, and so a kind of politician.

clue.text: A large bra size alternative – candidate's up for it!

definitions.note: a cryptic description: what a would-be candidate is up for, a noun in effect

blocks.note: taken as written
a D cup is a large bra size
an option is an alternative choice

explanation.surface: A saucy line about a generously endowed parliamentary hopeful who is up for anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up for it' suggests sexual eagerness, but here a would-be candidate is up for selection by a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A local party's formal choice of its election candidate is called adoption, which a hopeful candidate stands for.

clue.text: Exhibiting your majesty in gallery being gobbled by Stallone?

indicators.note: what is gobbled ends up inside the eater, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: Sylvester Stallone's nickname is Sly
the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: A query about Sylvester Stallone swallowing a portrait of the monarch in an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Your majesty' sounds like a form of address, but here it simply means dignified grandeur.
explanation.definitionFit: Stately means grand and dignified in manner, the bearing associated with majesty.

clue.text: City gets publicity: "Tory minister goes topless!"

indicators.note: going topless means losing the top, so the first letter of the name is removed

blocks.note: PR is public relations, publicity
William Hague was a Conservative cabinet minister

explanation.surface: A tabloid splash about a Conservative minister baring all on a city visit.
explanation.walkthrough: William Hague, former Tory leader and Foreign Secretary, loses his H.
explanation.definitionFit: Prague is the capital city of the Czech Republic.

clue.text: Be excessively fond of (after one 'E' and cocaine) a story

indicators.note: after tells us the bracketed letters come first and the fondness follows them

blocks.note: an, the indefinite article, means one
taken as written; E is also slang for ecstasy
C is slang for cocaine
to dote is to be overly fond

explanation.surface: Getting overly affectionate after a pill of ecstasy and some cocaine makes a good tale.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a short amusing story about a real incident.

clue.text: (& 15ac.) Coupling on TV: after dominatrix-fashion orgasm, political party enters sound as a bell

indicators.note: after places the climax word behind the dominatrix word in the line-up
something that enters goes inside, so the party is placed within the bell sound

blocks.note: a dominatrix acts severely, that is strictly
vulgar slang for an orgasm
ding is the ringing sound a bell makes
the African National Congress, South Africa's governing party

explanation.surface: A smutty description of sex on television, with a dominatrix and a politician involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound as a bell' normally means healthy; here it is the noise a bell makes.
explanation.definitionFit: Strictly Come Dancing is the BBC ballroom dance show in which celebrities are paired with professional partners.

clue.text: Having got an erection – shame – difficult to control

blocks.note: slang for being aroused
as in 'what a shame', 'what a pity'

explanation.surface: An awkward moment of arousal that, sadly, cannot be managed.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppity describes someone self-assertive and refusing to know their place, hence unruly and hard to manage.

clue.text: Conservative way rejected – it could damage cabinet

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: a Tory is a member of the Conservative Party
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A political story about a Conservative policy being thrown out and harming the Cabinet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cabinet' looks like the government's top ministers, but here it is a piece of wooden furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry rot is a fungus that decays timber, so it could ruin a wooden cupboard.

clue.text: "Hitler Ken" moving to seize Mayor's main seat of power

indicators.note: moving letters around shifts them into a new arrangement
main suggests the principal or leading part, so only the head letter is kept
seizing something means holding it within, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
the initial of mayor

explanation.surface: Ken Livingstone, 'Red Ken', cast as a dictator plotting to grab the Mayor of London's office.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Livingstone, a left-wing Mayor of London, was nicknamed Red Ken, which makes the Kremlin a sly fit.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kremlin is the Moscow fortress housing the Russian government, so it stands for the seat of power.

clue.text: Dicky's back covered in horrible bulge that's green

indicators.note: back means the word is turned to run backwards
something covered in another is wrapped inside it
a horrible shape is a misshapen one, so these letters are twisted out of order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
dicky is British slang for unwell or shaky, as in a dicky heart

explanation.surface: Someone called Dicky has an unpleasant growth on his back that has turned green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a name (or worse), but it is the British adjective meaning poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means inexperienced and naive, which is what a gullible person is: easily fooled.

clue.text: see 4dn.
see 10ac.
Kiss unusually large copper on behind

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means sitting on top of, so the earlier piece comes first

blocks.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing label for very large sizes
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
late means behind schedule

explanation.surface: A smooch from a big policeman on someone's bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' tempts as a backside and 'copper' as a policeman; here they are lateness and a chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: To osculate is a formal or jocular word meaning to kiss.

clue.text: He outs member publicly as tawdry queen

blocks.note: flash means showy and vulgar
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A gossip writer exposing a gay MP is condemned as a cheap old queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outs member' suggests revealing a party member's sexuality; the member is the male organ.
explanation.definitionFit: A flasher is a man who exposes his genitals in public.

clue.text: Realm riddled with S and M, causing stir

indicators.note: riddled means shot full of holes, so the letters are shattered and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A country overrun by sadomasochism, causing a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stir' looks like a verb or a fuss, but it is British slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir and slammer are both slang words for a prison or jail.

clue.text: Parliamentary knocker is deeply depressed at bar

blocks.note: as in a black mood
a rod is a bar

explanation.surface: A Westminster critic sits gloomily drinking in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Black Rod is the House of Lords official who knocks on the Commons door at the State Opening of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The holder of this office famously bangs on the closed door of the Commons with an ebony staff.

clue.text: Elected flipping pisspoor "non-Conservative Clegg" – bother!

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the word is read backwards
non- means without, so the abbreviation for a Conservative is taken out
something pisspoor is a shoddy mess, so the remaining letters are scrambled

blocks.note: a candidate who is elected is in
Nick Clegg, the Liberal Democrat leader

explanation.surface: A disgruntled voter grumbles about electing the useless coalition partner Nick Clegg.
explanation.walkthrough: C is the abbreviation for Conservative, removed from Clegg. 'Flipping' reads as a mild curse but turns the letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: To niggle is to irritate or trouble someone in a small but persistent way.

clue.text: Gutless bloke penetrated by arse's cross

indicators.note: without guts means the inside is emptied, so the middle letter goes
something penetrated has another thing pushed inside it

blocks.note: a guy is a man
the rump is the backside

explanation.surface: A crude image of a feeble man being sodomised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' could be a noun, but the 's means 'is' and cross is the adjective for angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Grumpy and cross both mean bad-tempered and irritable.

clue.text: Last pair of Gurkhas and Lumley dancing without lingerie elasticated tops – bedlam

indicators.note: only the final two letters of the word are taken
without means lacking, so those letters are removed
tops are the leading letters of the two following words
letters that dance move about into a new order

blocks.note: the final pair of letters of this word
Joanna Lumley, actress and campaigner for Gurkha rights
the opening letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Joanna Lumley dancing with Gurkhas, minus her underwear, causes chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: Joanna Lumley led the 2009 campaign for Gurkha veterans' right to settle in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedlam was a London lunatic asylum, and its name became a byword for madhouse chaos.

clue.text: Ed Miliband? Lost: "there's nothing in stupid bum rap!"

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for lost in sports results tables
nothing is zero, the letter O
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ed Miliband, having lost, complains his unfair reputation is baseless.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks Ed Miliband as one example. A bum rap is an unfair accusation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ed Miliband, a former Labour leader, is an example of a Labour member of Parliament.
